#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Global Smartwatch Secondary Market Analysis — Q1 2026 Generates a self-contained HTML report from data.csv """ import pandas as pd import numpy as np import matplotlib matplotlib.use('Agg') import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import matplotlib.ticker as mticker import base64 from io import BytesIO from pathlib import Path # ── Configuration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── DATA_PATH = '/app/benchmark/data.csv' OUTPUT_PATH = '/app/output/final_report.html' PRIMARY = '#1a365d' SECONDARY = '#4a5568' ACCENT_APPLE = '#007AFF' ACCENT_GARMIN = '#00A86B' ACCENT_SAMSUNG = '#1428A0' BRAND_COLORS = {'Apple': ACCENT_APPLE, 'Garmin': ACCENT_GARMIN, 'Samsung': ACCENT_SAMSUNG} PALETTE = ['#1a365d', '#2b6cb0', '#4299e1', '#63b3ed', '#90cdf4', '#bee3f8'] plt.rcParams.update({ 'font.family': 'sans-serif', 'font.size': 11, 'axes.titlesize': 13, 'axes.titleweight': 'bold', 'axes.labelsize': 11, 'figure.facecolor': 'white', 'axes.facecolor': '#f8fafc', 'axes.grid': True, 'grid.alpha': 0.3, 'grid.color': '#cbd5e0', }) # ── Data Loading & Cleaning ────────────────────────────────────────────────── def load_and_clean(): df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH) # Standardize country names country_map = { 'Estados Unidos': 'United States', 'Reino Unido': 'United Kingdom', 'Corea del Sur': 'South Korea', 'Italia': 'Italy', } df['Country'] = df['Country'].replace(country_map) # Standardize condition values cond_map = { 'Nuevo': 'New', 'Usado': 'Used', 'Caja abierta': 'Open box', 'Novo': 'New', '--': 'Used', } df['condition'] = df['condition'].replace(cond_map) # Filter to the three major brands df = df[df['brand'].isin(['Apple', 'Garmin', 'Samsung'])].copy() return df def fig_to_base64(fig, dpi=150): buf = BytesIO() fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=dpi, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white') buf.seek(0) b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode('utf-8') plt.close(fig) return b64 # ── Section 1: Market Overview ──────────────────────────────────────────────── def section_market_overview(df): total = len(df) brand_counts = df['brand'].value_counts() cond_counts = df['condition'].value_counts() country_counts = df['Country'].value_counts() unique_sellers = df['Seller_ID'].nunique() # KPI row kpis = { 'Total Listings': f'{total:,}', 'Brands Covered': '3 (Apple, Garmin, Samsung)', 'Countries': str(df['Country'].nunique()), 'Unique Sellers': f'{unique_sellers:,}', 'Median Price': f'${df["price"].median():,.0f}', 'Price Range': f'${df["price"].min():,.0f} – ${df["price"].max():,.0f}', } # Brand distribution pie chart fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4)) wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie( brand_counts.values, labels=brand_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=[BRAND_COLORS[b] for b in brand_counts.index], startangle=90, textprops={'fontsize': 11}, ) for t in autotexts: t.set_color('white') t.set_fontweight('bold') ax.set_title('Listing Distribution by Brand') fig.tight_layout() brand_pie_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # Condition distribution bar main_conds = cond_counts[cond_counts >= 10] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5)) bars = ax.barh(main_conds.index[::-1], main_conds.values[::-1], color=PALETTE[:len(main_conds)]) ax.set_xlabel('Number of Listings') ax.set_title('Listing Count by Condition') for bar in bars: w = bar.get_width() ax.text(w + 15, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'{int(w):,}', va='center', fontsize=9) fig.tight_layout() cond_bar_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # Top countries bar top_countries = country_counts.head(10) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5)) bars = ax.barh(top_countries.index[::-1], top_countries.values[::-1], color=PALETTE[1]) ax.set_xlabel('Number of Listings') ax.set_title('Top 10 Countries by Listing Volume') for bar in bars: w = bar.get_width() ax.text(w + 10, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'{int(w):,}', va='center', fontsize=9) fig.tight_layout() country_bar_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # Brand x Condition table brand_cond = df.groupby(['brand', 'condition']).size().unstack(fill_value=0) main_cond_cols = ['New', 'Used', 'Open box'] for c in main_cond_cols: if c not in brand_cond.columns: brand_cond[c] = 0 brand_cond = brand_cond[main_cond_cols] brand_cond['Total'] = brand_cond.sum(axis=1) return { 'kpis': kpis, 'brand_counts': brand_counts, 'cond_counts': cond_counts, 'country_counts': country_counts, 'brand_cond': brand_cond, 'brand_pie_b64': brand_pie_b64, 'cond_bar_b64': cond_bar_b64, 'country_bar_b64': country_bar_b64, } # ── Section 2: Brand-Level Pricing & Value Retention ───────────────────────── def section_brand_pricing(df): stats = df.groupby('brand')['price'].agg(['mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'count']) stats = stats.round(2) stats.columns = ['Mean ($)', 'Median ($)', 'Std Dev ($)', 'Min ($)', 'Max ($)', 'Count'] # Median price by brand bar fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4)) brands = stats.index.tolist() medians = stats['Median ($)'].values colors = [BRAND_COLORS[b] for b in brands] bars = ax.bar(brands, medians, color=colors, width=0.5) for bar, val in zip(bars, medians): ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 8, f'${val:,.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold', fontsize=11) ax.set_ylabel('Median Price (USD)') ax.set_title('Median Resale Price by Brand') ax.set_ylim(0, max(medians) * 1.15) fig.tight_layout() median_bar_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # Price distribution violin/box fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5)) brand_data = [df[df['brand'] == b]['price'].values for b in brands] bp = ax.boxplot(brand_data, labels=brands, patch_artist=True, showfliers=False, medianprops=dict(color='white', linewidth=2)) for patch, b in zip(bp['boxes'], brands): patch.set_facecolor(BRAND_COLORS[b]) patch.set_alpha(0.85) ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)') ax.set_title('Price Distribution by Brand (outliers excluded)') fig.tight_layout() box_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # Mean price by brand & condition cond_brand = df[df['condition'].isin(['New', 'Used'])].groupby(['brand', 'condition'])['price'].mean().unstack() fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4)) x = np.arange(len(brands)) w = 0.3 new_vals = [cond_brand.loc[b, 'New'] if b in cond_brand.index else 0 for b in brands] used_vals = [cond_brand.loc[b, 'Used'] if b in cond_brand.index else 0 for b in brands] ax.bar(x - w/2, new_vals, w, label='New', color='#2b6cb0') ax.bar(x + w/2, used_vals, w, label='Used', color='#90cdf4') ax.set_xticks(x) ax.set_xticklabels(brands) ax.set_ylabel('Mean Price (USD)') ax.set_title('Mean Price: New vs. Used by Brand') ax.legend() fig.tight_layout() cond_compare_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # KPI: New vs Used premium premium_by_brand = {} for b in brands: new_p = df[(df['brand'] == b) & (df['condition'] == 'New')]['price'].mean() used_p = df[(df['brand'] == b) & (df['condition'] == 'Used')]['price'].mean() if used_p > 0: premium_by_brand[b] = ((new_p - used_p) / used_p) * 100 else: premium_by_brand[b] = 0 return { 'stats': stats, 'median_bar_b64': median_bar_b64, 'box_b64': box_b64, 'cond_compare_b64': cond_compare_b64, 'premium_by_brand': premium_by_brand, } # ── Section 3: Geographic Pricing Arbitrage ─────────────────────────────────── def section_geospatial(df): # Only countries with >= 10 listings for reliability country_counts = df['Country'].value_counts() valid_countries = country_counts[country_counts >= 10].index.tolist() df_geo = df[df['Country'].isin(valid_countries)].copy() # Median price by country and brand pivot = df_geo.groupby(['Country', 'brand'])['price'].median().unstack() pivot = pivot.reindex(columns=['Apple', 'Garmin', 'Samsung']) # Global median per brand global_medians = df.groupby('brand')['price'].median() # Percentage deviation from global median deviation = pd.DataFrame(index=pivot.index) for b in ['Apple', 'Garmin', 'Samsung']: deviation[b] = ((pivot[b] - global_medians[b]) / global_medians[b]) * 100 # Geographic Price Spread KPI geo_spread = {} for b in ['Apple', 'Garmin', 'Samsung']: country_medians = df_geo[df_geo['brand'] == b].groupby('Country')['price'].median() if len(country_medians) >= 2: geo_spread[b] = country_medians.max() - country_medians.min() else: geo_spread[b] = 0 # Heatmap of deviation fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, max(4, len(deviation) * 0.45))) dev_sorted = deviation.sort_values('Apple', ascending=False) im = ax.imshow(dev_sorted.values, cmap='RdBu_r', aspect='auto', vmin=-40, vmax=40) ax.set_xticks(range(3)) ax.set_xticklabels(['Apple', 'Garmin', 'Samsung']) ax.set_yticks(range(len(dev_sorted))) ax.set_yticklabels(dev_sorted.index) for i in range(len(dev_sorted)): for j in range(3): val = dev_sorted.iloc[i, j] if pd.notna(val): color = 'white' if abs(val) > 20 else 'black' ax.text(j, i, f'{val:+.1f}%', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9, color=color) cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label='% Deviation from Global Median') ax.set_title('Geographic Price Deviation from Global Median (%)') fig.tight_layout() heatmap_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # Country median price bar chart for each brand fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(14, 5), sharey=False) for idx, b in enumerate(['Apple', 'Garmin', 'Samsung']): ax = axes[idx] brand_country = df_geo[df_geo['brand'] == b].groupby('Country')['price'].median().sort_values(ascending=True) if len(brand_country) > 0: colors_pos = ['#e53e3e' if v > global_medians[b] else '#2b6cb0' for v in brand_country.values] bars = ax.barh(brand_country.index, brand_country.values, color=colors_pos, height=0.6) ax.axvline(global_medians[b], color='black', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, label=f'Global Median ${global_medians[b]:,.0f}') ax.set_title(b, color=BRAND_COLORS[b], fontweight='bold') ax.set_xlabel('Median Price (USD)') if idx == 0: ax.set_ylabel('') ax.legend(fontsize=8) fig.suptitle('Median Price by Country & Brand (Red = Above Global Median)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', y=1.02) fig.tight_layout() country_bar_b64 = fig_to_base64(fig) # Top arbitrage opportunities table arb_data = [] for b in ['Apple', 'Garmin', 'Samsung']: country_medians = df_geo[df_geo['brand'] == b].groupby('Country')['price'].median().dropna() if len(country_medians) >= 2: cheapest = country_medians.idxmin() priciest = country_medians.idxmax() spread = country_medians.max() - country_medians.min() arb_data.append({ 'Brand': b, 'Cheapest Country': cheapest, 'Median Price (Low)': f'${country_medians[cheapest]:,.0f}', 'Priciest Country': priciest, 'Median Price (High)': f'${country_medians[priciest]:,.0f}', 'Spread (USD)': f'${spread:,.0f}', }) arb_df = pd.DataFrame(arb_data) return { 'pivot': pivot, 'deviation': deviation, 'geo_spread': geo_spread, 'global_medians': global_medians, 'heatmap_b64': heatmap_b64, 'country_bar_b64': country_bar_b64, 'arb_df': arb_df, 'valid_countries': valid_countries, } #
